scope: Two teaching codes inspired by narrative coding; not the project's nine-trope codebook.
unit: Prepared segment interpreted in its document context
multi_label: Both may occur if the text supports distinct mechanisms; defend each assignment.

concealed_reversal.name: Concealment followed by revelation
concealed_reversal.definition: A story in which a favorable public appearance gives way to a damaging reversal.
include: Identify an appearance and a later damaging reversal; the role of concealment needs collective clarification.
exclude: Static criticism without an event sequence.
concealed_reversal.uncertainty: Preserve uncertainty if the actor, sequence, or author's stance cannot be resolved from the available context.

structural_trap.name: Self-defeating operating sequence
structural_trap.definition: The passage advances an event sequence in which the operating arrangement itself produces a worsening consequence even as actors follow it.
include: Name the repeated or linked actions, the arrangement connecting them, and the worsening consequence.
exclude: A bad outcome alone, a static unfavorable ratio, or a single execution mistake.
A mechanism the author quotes only to reject.
structural_trap.uncertainty: Retain rival interpretations of mechanism and temporality.
